meaning:
εὐ-οδόω, -ῶ
(ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for צָלַח hi. ;]
to help on one's way (Soph., al.). Pass., to have a prosperous journey; metaphorically (Hdt., al.), to prosper, be prospered, be successful: 3Jn.2, Rom.1:10, 1Co.16:2 (on the tense, see M, Pr., 54; ICC, in l).†
(AS)

renderings.kjv: I might have a prosperous journey

elsewhere.note: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.
On the first day of every week, let each one of you save, as he may prosper, that no collections are made when I come.
Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be healthy, even as your soul prospers.
